arxiv-2112-01068.title: The Packet Number Space Debate in Multipath QUIC
arxiv-2112-01068.creator: Quentin De Coninck
arxiv-2112-01068.description: Abstract . With a standardization process that attracted many interest, QUIC can been seen as the next general-purpose transport protocol. Still, it does not provide true multipath support yet, missing some use cases that MPTCP can address. To fill that gap, the IETF recently adopted a multipath proposal merging all the proposed designs.

arxiv-2205-08778.title: Accuracy Enhancement for Ear Acoustic Authentication Using Between-class Features
arxiv-2205-08778.creator: Masaki YASUHARA, Isao Nambu, Yoshiko MARUYAMA, Shohei YANO
arxiv-2205-08778.description: Abstract In existing biometric authentication methods, the user must perform an authentication operation such as placing a finger in a scanner or facing a camera. With ear acoustic authentication, acoustic characteristics of the ear canal are used as biometric information. Therefore, a person wearing earphones does not need to perform any authentication operation.

arxiv-2210-00628.title: Origin of degenerate bound states in the continuum in a grating waveguide: Parity symmetry breaking due to mode crossing
arxiv-2210-00628.creator: C.B. Reynolds, Vl.V. Kocharovsky, V.V. Kocharovsky Department of Physics and Astronomy, Texas A&M University, College Station, TX 77843, USA
arxiv-2210-00628.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by C.B. Reynolds, Vl.V. Kocharovsky, V.V. Kocharovsky Department of Physics and Astronomy, Texas A&M University, College Station, TX 77843, USA. We explain the origin of bound states in the continuum (BICs) in a planar grating waveguide, in particular, a mechanism for formation of degenerate BICs, via the analytical theory of the infinite-grating eigenmodes. Conventional symmetry-protected BICs are formed at normal incidence mainly by a single infinite-grating eigenmode that has an odd spatial parity on both sides of the BIC resonance.

arxiv-2210-16465.title: Efficient Mean-Field Simulation of Quantum Circuits Inspired by Density Functional Theory
arxiv-2210-16465.creator: Marco Bernardi
arxiv-2210-16465.description: Abstract \vskip12.0pt Exact simulations of quantum circuits (QCs) are currently limited to ∼ \sim 50 qubits because the memory and computational cost required to store the QC wave function scale exponentially with qubit number. Therefore, developing efficient schemes for approximate QC simulations is a current research focus.

arxiv-2307-04593.title: DWA: Differential Wavelet Amplifier for Image Super-Resolution
arxiv-2307-04593.creator: Brian B. Moser, Stanislav Frolov, Federico Raue, Sebastian Palacio, Andreas Dengel
arxiv-2307-04593.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Brian B. Moser, Stanislav Frolov, Federico Raue, Sebastian Palacio, Andreas Dengel. This work introduces Differential Wavelet Amplifier (DWA), a drop-in module for wavelet-based image Super-Resolution (SR). DWA invigorates an approach recently receiving less attention, namely Discrete Wavelet Transformation (DWT). DWT enables an efficient image representation for SR and reduces the spatial area of its input by a factor of 4, the overall model size, and computation cost, framing it as an attractive approach for sustainable ML.

arxiv-2409-00170.title: Discovering Dark Matter with the MUonE Experiment
arxiv-2409-00170.creator: Gordan Krnjaic, Duncan Rocha, Isaac R. Wang
arxiv-2409-00170.description: Abstract The MUonE experiment aims to extract the hadronic contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment from a precise measurement of the muon-electron differential scattering cross section. We show that MUonE can also discover thermal relic dark matter using only its nominal experimental setup.

arxiv-2412-01951.title: Self-Improvement in Language Models: The Sharpening Mechanism
arxiv-2412-01951.creator: Audrey Huang audreyh5@illinois.edu Adam Block blockadam@microsoft.com Dylan J. Foster dylanfoster@microsoft.com Dhruv Rohatgi drohatgi@mit.edu and Cyril Zhang cyrilzhang@microsoft.com Max Simchowitz msimchow@andrew.cmu.edu Jordan T. Ash ash.jordan@microsoft.com Akshay Krishnamurthy akshaykr@microsof
arxiv-2412-01951.description: Abstract Recent work in language modeling has raised the possibility of self-improvement , where a language models evaluates and refines its own generations to achieve higher performance without external feedback. It is impossible for this self-improvement to create information that is not already in the model, so why should we expect that this will lead to improved capabilities?

pmc-10736823.title: EVALUATING THE BEHAVIORAL RECOVERY OUTREACH (BRO) TEAM MODEL: TEAM MEMBERS’ PERSPECTIVES
pmc-10736823.creator: Amanda Peeples, Elizabeth MacDonald, Kathleen Matthews
pmc-10736823.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The VA’s Behavioral Recovery Outreach (BRO) Team model seeks to address the unmet needs of aging Veterans with complex behavioral, psychological, neurocognitive, and medical concerns. Consisting of a core team of a social worker, nurse, and psychologist, BRO teams collaborate with the broader VA Community Living Center or inpatient team on behavioral assessment and treatment planning to help stabilize the Veterans’ behaviors and ready them for discharge to the community.

pmc-13068277.title: Implementation barriers of Brazil’s national home visitation program for early childhood development: A qualitative evaluation
pmc-13068277.creator: Christopher M. Westgard, Ana Carolina Silva Onofre, Nayara Vieira Peres, Luana Bessa, Ana Luiza Raggio Colagrossi, Jaqueline Lima Santos, Diego Fontana Siqueira Cunha, Alexandra Brentani
pmc-13068277.description: This research delves into the challenges faced in implementing home visitation programs for early childhood development, focusing on the Programa Criança Feliz (PCF) in Brazil. We aimed to better understand what barriers are hindering PCF from creating a greater positive impact on its primary outcomes. This is a cross-sectional qualitative study.

pmc-13083861.title: Single-cell and multi-omics analysis identifies mitophagy-related biomarkers and therapeutic targets in ischemic stroke
pmc-13083861.creator: Zhan Cao, Yingluan Wang, Mingjian Sun, Runyi Du, Xu Feng, Lin Wang, Ziyi Zhao, Wei Sun
pmc-13083861.description: Ischemic stroke (IS) remains a leading cause of death and disability, with limited effective treatments in the acute phase. Mitophagy, the selective degradation of damaged mitochondria, plays a crucial role in cellular homeostasis and survival during IS. However, its exact mechanisms in stroke pathophysiology remain unclear.

pmc-13116222.title: Human iPSC‐derived GABAergic interneuron transplantation restores circuit balance and cognitive function in an Alzheimer's disease model

pmc-13394024.creator: Shinya Abe, Hiroaki Nozawa, Kentaro Abe, Yumi Yokota, Shunsuke Hori, Yusuke Taguchi, Mitsutaka Yakabe, Kazuhito Sasaki, Sumito Ogawa, Soichiro Ishihara
pmc-13394024.description: IntroductionPreoperative chemoradiotherapy (CRT) for rectal cancer may have an attritional impact on body composition and functional status, affecting postoperative outcomes. pmc-13462590.title: Asymmetric structural transitions in the icosahedral organization of Eastern equine encephalitis virus
pmc-13462590.creator: Abhishek Bandyopadhyay, Lauren E. Williamson, Cameron D. Buchman, Thomas Klose, James E. Crowe, Richard J. Kuhn
pmc-13462590.description: Delivery of the viral genome into host cells is a critical step in successful viral infection. Alphaviruses achieve this step by fusing the viral and endosomal membranes under acidic conditions. This process requires significant structural changes in the alphavirus glycoprotein organization.
